categories.main_business_segments: Matsuya Foods Holdings operates primarily in the restaurant business, focusing on Japanese-style fast food chains such as 'Matsuya' (beef bowl and set meals), 'Matsunoya' (tonkatsu), 'My Curry Shokudo' (curry), as well as sushi, Chinese, steak, pasta, and cafe concepts. The group manages both directly operated and franchise stores, with a single business segment centered on food service.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes a central kitchen system, processing key ingredients (meat, rice, sauces, vegetables) at four main production and logistics centers in Japan. It emphasizes food safety, efficient supply chain management, and automation/mechanization in production and logistics. The group also invests in digital ordering systems (ticket machines) and is advancing sustainability initiatives such as food waste recycling and solar power installations.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The main customers are general consumers seeking affordable, quick-service meals, including individuals, families, and office workers. The company targets a broad demographic in Japan and increasingly serves inbound tourists and overseas customers through its international expansion in East Asia.
categories.geographic_coverage: Matsuya Foods Holdings operates 1,342 stores across 44 prefectures in Japan and 23 stores overseas (mainly in Taiwan, China, and Hong Kong). The majority of revenue is generated in Japan, with growing presence in East Asian markets.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company is positioned downstream in the supply chain as a food service retailer, directly serving end consumers through its restaurant network. It also manages upstream activities such as food processing and logistics through its own factories and distribution centers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding store count (especially new formats and overseas), remodeling existing stores, investing in human capital, and enhancing customer convenience through digitalization. R&D focuses on new menu development, food safety, and sustainability (notably food waste recycling and climate change response). The company is also pursuing M&A opportunities and strengthening its ESG initiatives.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated from direct sales of food and beverages at company-operated restaurants, supplemented by franchise royalties, sales of food materials and consumables to franchisees, and some external sales (e.g., maintenance, cleaning services). Franchisees pay initial fees, deposits, royalties (1-5% of sales), and advertising contributions.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include other major Japanese fast food and quick-service restaurant chains such as Yoshinoya, Sukiya (Zensho Holdings), and other multi-brand food service groups. Matsuya Foods Holdings is a leading player in the beef bowl and set meal segment, with a strong domestic network and a growing international footprint.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended March 2025, consolidated sales reached ¥154.2 billion, with operating profit of ¥4.4 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥2.19 billion. The company has shown strong top-line growth (20.9% YoY), driven by new store openings and recovery in existing store sales, though profitability has been pressured by rising costs. Total assets are ¥104.2 billion, and the group employs over 2,100 regular staff and 10,000+ part-time workers.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Matsuya Foods Holdings differentiates itself through a commitment to safety, quality, and value, offering a wide variety of affordable, freshly prepared meals with fast service. The company emphasizes customer convenience (e.g., digital ordering), menu innovation, and sustainability (food waste recycling, low-carbon operations), aiming to be 'everyone's dining table' and a trusted, accessible brand for diverse customer needs.
